Audits · Usage

Real user testing

Your journeys, tested by the people who need them most.

An audit measures compliance; user testing reveals the lived experience. We run sessions with people with visual, motor, hearing or cognitive disabilities, who use their own tools on your key journeys.

Request a quoteIn detail

At a glance

Participants
People with disabilities, expert users of their tools
Format
One-to-one sessions, on site or remote
Deliverables
Findings, quotes and prioritised recommendations
Best with
An RGAA, RAAM or compliance audit

When to test?

Before going live

To fix major barriers before they reach your users.

After an audit

To check that the fixes really make the journey usable.

On high-stakes services

Administrative procedures, payment, booking, customer account.

What the test includes

  1. 01Participant recruitmentProfiles chosen according to your audiences and journeys.
  2. 02Test scenariosRealistic tasks, built with your teams.
  3. 03Observed sessionsEach participant completes the tasks with a consultant.
  4. 04Assistive technologiesScreen readers, braille displays, magnification, voice control, switches.
  5. 05Barrier analysisObstacles ranked by severity, with their technical cause.
  6. 06Team debriefConcrete findings that help the whole team understand what is at stake.

Frequently asked questions

How many participants are needed?

It depends on the profiles to cover and the journeys tested. We propose a number during scoping.

Can sessions be recorded?

Yes, with the participants’ consent, to share excerpts with your teams.

Can a prototype be tested?

Yes, as soon as the journey can be used on an interactive mock-up or a test build.

Is user testing enough to be compliant?

No. It complements the audit, which remains the reference measure of compliance.
